editable.overview::p::0: The MCD is a standard set of loan data fields and delivery file format that mortgage lenders and independent mortgage banks provide to regulators for the loan-level review portion of regulatory compliance examinations. It's designed to replace the Loan Examination File (LEF).
editable.overview::p::1: Lenders and regulators can test a single loan or an entire portfolio against the MCD — lenders to cure defects before an exam, regulators to run the exam itself.
editable.why-card::li::0: Manual, inconsistent reviews slow examinations down. Regulators examine individual loans against consumer-protection rules (disclosures, ability-to-repay, points and fees, high-cost mortgages, and more) largely by hand, without a standard format to run technology against.
editable.why-card::li::1: Inconsistent formats break compliance technology. For automated review to work across the industry, data submissions need one common structure, fields, names, and enumerations — a shared language for regulators, lenders, and vendors.
editable.why-card::li::2: Lenders want to catch issues before the exam. The same standard that lets regulators run risk-based reviews lets lenders test their own portfolios and cure defects ahead of time.
editable.overview::span::5: MISMO, in partnership with the Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS)
editable.overview::span::7: To replace the inconsistent Loan Examination File (LEF) format with a standardized compliance dataset that lenders and regulators could test loans against consistently.
